judged_text: The booking-update path fetches a credential by reference.credentialId via prisma.credential.findUnique with no ownership check and passes it to updateEvent, so a booking reference carrying a foreign credentialId executes authenticated calendar updates as the victim. A booking whose calendar reference stores a planted foreign credentialId (references inherit credentialId from the destinationCalendar used at creation) makes reschedule/update run with the victim's OAuth credential against the victim's calendar, modifying events the attacker's booking has no right to touch.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The booking-update path fetches a credential by reference.credentialId via prisma.credential.findUnique with no ownership check and passes it to updateEvent, so a booking reference carrying a foreign credentialId executes authenticated calendar updates as the victim. A booking whose calendar reference stores a planted foreign credentialId (references inherit credentialId from the destinationCalendar used at creation) makes reschedule/update run with the victim's OAuth credential against the victim's calendar, modifying events the attacker's booking has no right to touch.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the booking update path now falls back to fetching a credential directly from the DB when it can’t be found in `this.calendarCredentials`: `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })`, then constructs a `credential` object and calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` (same pattern also added in `createAllCalendarEvents`). The diff shows no check that the fetched credential belongs to the booking’s organizer/user/team (no `userId`/`teamId` validation against the booking context). That means any booking reference containing an arbitrary `credentialId` would cause calendar updates/deletes to run using that credential’s OAuth, which is a privilege escalation if an attacker can get a foreign `credentialId` into a booking reference.
